Suvadu 0.5.2 is a distribution release: Suvadu installs the same way however you get it, `cargo binstall` fetches the signed pre-built binaries, and the MCP server is ready for the official MCP Registry. There are no changes to recording, search or the database.
- **The database upgrades itself** on the first run (schema v16), building its new search indexes once: under a second for 100,000 commands.

Suvadu 0.5.0 adds Home, a searchable map of everything Suvadu does, and reworks recall around finding a command: identical commands grouped with when each last ran, and matches highlighted. The install script can now install without sudo, add the shell hook for you and verify the release signature.

### Added
- **Suvadu Home.** A bare `suv` at a terminal, or `suv home`, opens a searchable map of everything Suvadu does, grouped by task. Typing searches the features, not your history, and each shows the real

- **`suv doctor` no longer creates the database** as a side effect of checking for it, and `suv uninstall` prints the real config and data paths.
- **Atuin migration** — `suv import --from atuin-db <path/to/history.db>`, with `--dry-run`. The Atuin database is opened read-only; rows are identified by their Atuin id, so re-running does not duplicate.
- **Matching modes and recall scopes in `suv search`** — `--match terms|literal|prefix|fuzzy` (`^X`) chooses how a query matches; `--scope all|directory|wor

- `suv mcp-serve` no longer disconnects before completing the MCP handshake when the local database was already migrated to a newer schema by a different Suvadu build — every tool/resource call now reports the underlying database error instead of the connected host seeing an opaque "Connection closed".

A shared skills library lets any MCP-capable agent read reusable instructions instead of every tool duplicating its own copy, plus new safety tooling (`suv guard`, obfuscation detection, per-project config overrides) and a visual-consistency pass across every TUI screen.

### Added
- Shared skills library (`suv skills`) — reusable instructions any MCP-capable agent can discover and read. Interactive TUI to browse/add/edit/sync/review pending proposals; `add/list/show/edit/rm/sync` still work as scripting

Codex CLI joins Claude Code and Cursor as a first-class agent integration, plus a fix for a `.bashrc` history-recording bug.

### Added
- **Codex CLI is now a first-class agent integration** — `suv init codex` installs hooks that capture both prompts and shell commands, merging into any hooks you already have in `~/.codex/hooks.json` (synapse, plannotator, etc.) rather than overwriting them, and auto-registers the suvadu MCP server in `~/.codex/config.toml` so Codex can query your shell history directly.
